newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux blames markets/currency for profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux blames markets/currency for profit fall.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB said on Tuesday weak market conditions in all European business areas and negative currency effects were behind a 13 percent drop in profits for the first nine months of the year.
The group posted a 2.42 billion crown profit after financial items for the first three quarters of 1996, compared to 2.78 billion reported for the same period a year ago.
Electrolux blames currency for profit fall = 2
Sales for the period fell seven percent to 82.92 billion crowns, and Electrolux said currencies had been one of the main contributors to the fall.

"The stronger Swedish crown had an unfavourable effect on sales and income in connection with the translation of financial statements in foreign subsidiaries, and led to a decrease in balance sheet items," the company said in a statement.
The stronger Italian lira, an important income currency for Electrolux, had also been behind the fall, it added.

Weak performance from the industrial products business area -- which mainly consists of the Granges engineering unit -- were behind a 15 percent fall in operating income after depreciation to 3.32 billion crowns.

The commercial appliances division, which includes the group's commercial kitchen and laundry areas, and outdoor appliances, whose leading brands include Flymo and Husqvarna, also made a lower contribution.
However, the operating profit of Electrolux's flagship household appliances business area was largely unchanged on the same 1995 period at 1.73 billion crowns.
